children.text: A homogeneous zero-effective-length spring has mass \(M\), minimum and unstretched length \(L_0\), and tension \(F=kL\) when stretched to \(L>L_0\). It stays at \(L_0\) for smaller tensile forces. Define \(\alpha=kL_0/(Mg)<1\). Label material points by their unstretched distance \(0\le\ell\le L_0\) from the bottom. After release from hanging equilibrium, the spring contracts from the top. Its moving part forms a rigid chunk that collects stationary turns. Each lower point stays at rest until reached. Once the spring has collapsed to length \(L_0\), it falls as a rigid body without tumbling. Use this model, neglect air resistance, and retain finite \(L_0\).

children.text: A segment of unstretched length \(\Delta\ell\) is pulled by force \(F\) in weightlessness. Find its length \(\Delta y\).
Find work to extend that segment from \(\Delta\ell\) to \(\Delta y\ge\Delta\ell\).
Find the time \(t_c\) until the spring reaches length \(L_0\).
While a stretched stationary section exists, its mass is \(M\ell/L_0\). Show that the rigid moving section has speed \(v_I(\ell)=\sqrt{A\ell+B}\), and determine \(A,B\).
Find minimum speed before ground impact, using \(A,B,L_0,\alpha\).
Find the heat generated from release until just before ground impact.

statement.text:
Zero-length springs and slinky coils
A homogeneous zero-effective-length spring has mass \(M\), minimum and unstretched length \(L_0\), and tension \(F=kL\) when stretched to \(L>L_0\). It stays at \(L_0\) for smaller tensile forces. Define \(\alpha=kL_0/(Mg)<1\). Label material points by their unstretched distance \(0\le\ell\le L_0\) from the bottom. After release from hanging equilibrium, the spring contracts from the top. Its moving part forms a rigid chunk that collects stationary turns. Each lower point stays at rest until reached. Once the spring has collapsed to length \(L_0\), it falls as a rigid body without tumbling. Use this model, neglect air resistance, and retain finite \(L_0\).

A.1. Segment extension
A segment of unstretched length \(\Delta\ell\) is pulled by force \(F\) in weightlessness. Find its length \(\Delta y\).
A.2. Stretching work
Find work to extend that segment from \(\Delta\ell\) to \(\Delta y\ge\Delta\ell\).
A.3. Hanging length
Find the equilibrium total length \(H\).
B.1.formula. Collapse time
Find the time \(t_c\) until the spring reaches length \(L_0\).
B.1.value. Collapse time value
Evaluate for \(k=1.02\,\mathrm{N/m}\), \(L_0=0.055\,\mathrm m\), \(M=0.201\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(g=9.80\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\).
B.2. Moving-front velocity
While a stretched stationary section exists, its mass is \(M\ell/L_0\). Show that the rigid moving section has speed \(v_I(\ell)=\sqrt{A\ell+B}\), and determine \(A,B\).
B.3. Minimum moving speed
Find minimum speed before ground impact, using \(A,B,L_0,\alpha\).
C.1. Mechanical energy lost
Find the heat generated from release until just before ground impact.

children.text: Homogeneity gives an effective segment constant \(k_*=kL_0/\Delta\ell\). Thus \[\Delta y=\Delta\ell\max\left(1,\frac F{kL_0}\right).\]
Integrate the force \(k_*y\) from the minimum length: \[\Delta W=\frac{kL_0}{2\Delta\ell}(\Delta y^2-\Delta\ell^2).\]

Tension at material coordinate \(\ell\) is \(Mg\ell/L_0\). Turns remain touching up to \(\ell_0=\alpha L_0\). Above that, \(dy/d\ell=\ell/(\alpha L_0)\). Integrating both regions gives \[H=\frac{L_0}{2}(\alpha+1/\alpha).\]

The initial centre-of-mass height above the bottom is \(y_{cm}=L_0[1/(6\alpha)-\alpha^2/6+\alpha/2]\). At collapse it is \(L_0/2\), since the bottom has stayed at rest. The CM falls freely, so \(gt_c^2/2=y_{cm}-L_0/2=L_0(1-\alpha)^3/(6\alpha)\). Hence \[t_c=\sqrt{\frac{L_0(1-\alpha)^3}{3g\alpha}}.\]

Total downward momentum is \(Mgt\). The moving mass is \(M(1-\ell/L_0)\), so \((1-\ell/L_0)v_I=gt\). The boundary height is \(y(\ell)=\ell^2/(2\alpha L_0)+\alpha L_0/2\), and the moving chunk has length \(L_0-\ell\). Its top height therefore has derivative \(\ell/(\alpha L_0)-1\) with respect to \(\ell\). Combining the kinematic front speed with momentum gives \[v_I^2=\frac{2g}{3\alpha}\ell+gL_0\left(\frac1{3\alpha}-1\right).\] Thus \(A=2g/(3\alpha)\), \(B=gL_0[1/(3\alpha)-1]\). These apply for \(\alpha L_0<\ell<L_0\). The singular instantaneous start is a feature of the ideal collection model, not an initially nonzero speed of a finite mass.

The moving chunk slows until reaching the touching bottom section at \(\ell=\alpha L_0\). It then inelastically collects the bottom mass \(\alpha M\). Momentum conservation gives \[v_{min}=(1-\alpha)\sqrt{A\alpha L_0+B}.\] Subsequently the full spring accelerates downwards. This also equals \(gt_c\).

The CM gravitational energy decrease becomes its translational kinetic energy. All initial elastic energy is therefore lost to heat and other internal dissipation. Integrate the segment energy over the stretched part: \[Q=\int_{\alpha L_0}^{L_0}\frac{kL_0}{2}\left[\frac{\ell^2}{\alpha^2L_0^2}-1\right]d\ell=\frac{MgL_0(1-\alpha)^2(2\alpha+1)}{6\alpha}.\]

Zero-length springs and slinky coils
A.1. Segment extension
Homogeneity gives an effective segment constant \(k_*=kL_0/\Delta\ell\). Thus \[\Delta y=\Delta\ell\max\left(1,\frac F{kL_0}\right).\]
A.2. Stretching work
Integrate the force \(k_*y\) from the minimum length: \[\Delta W=\frac{kL_0}{2\Delta\ell}(\Delta y^2-\Delta\ell^2).\]
A.3. Hanging length
Tension at material coordinate \(\ell\) is \(Mg\ell/L_0\). Turns remain touching up to \(\ell_0=\alpha L_0\). Above that, \(dy/d\ell=\ell/(\alpha L_0)\). Integrating both regions gives \[H=\frac{L_0}{2}(\alpha+1/\alpha).\]

B.1.value. Collapse time value
\(\alpha=0.0285\), giving \(t_c=0.245\,\mathrm s\).
B.2. Moving-front velocity
Total downward momentum is \(Mgt\). The moving mass is \(M(1-\ell/L_0)\), so \((1-\ell/L_0)v_I=gt\). The boundary height is \(y(\ell)=\ell^2/(2\alpha L_0)+\alpha L_0/2\), and the moving chunk has length \(L_0-\ell\). These apply for \(\alpha L_0<\ell<L_0\). The singular instantaneous start is a feature of the ideal collection model, not an initially nonzero speed of a finite mass.
B.3. Minimum moving speed
The moving chunk slows until reaching the touching bottom section at \(\ell=\alpha L_0\). It then inelastically collects the bottom mass \(\alpha M\). Momentum conservation gives \[v_{min}=(1-\alpha)\sqrt{A\alpha L_0+B}.\] Subsequently the full spring accelerates downwards. This also equals \(gt_c\).
